account:
Today I have followed my appointments: morning correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, and the town accounts. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury. The secretary had removed the appointment book earlier, so the appointments chest was empty when I checked again. The secretary confirmed my three o'clock tea and my next office appointment at four thirty. I have now arrived at the neighbour's dockside cottage just after three, and the neighbour is waiting nearby.

The unusual recurring news is about the baker carrying a sack of bread. Several townsfolk reported seeing this at the inn, and later others reported it at the north side of the plaza. I also personally saw freight give the baker an emerald at about 14:09. This could be ordinary bread sales or deliveries, but I do not know the purpose or quantity involved, nor whether the reports refer to separate trips. Repeated reports alone do not establish anything improper. The baker and freight are the people directly connected to what I have observed; the townsfolk have been spreading their sightings. Tea is an opportunity to hear what the neighbour has noticed, while keeping these observations distinct from speculation.
